The file `30-sdmx/output/structures/AFW360_structures.xml` is an SDMX-ML 3.1 structure
message. It is generated by `30-sdmx/pipeline/build_sdmx.R` from `30-sdmx/data/metadata/`, so you
never edit it by hand. Its core is the **Data Structure Definition (DSD)**
`WB.AFW360:DSD_AFW360_HH(0.3.0)`. Everything else in the file either feeds the
DSD or points at it.

## What a DSD does

A DSD is the schema for every number in `data/*.csv`. It says three things:

1. **Which columns identify an observation** (the *dimensions*, together called
   the "key").
2. **Which columns hold numbers** (the *measures*).
3. **Which columns describe a number without identifying it** (the
   *attributes*).

It also ties each column to a **concept** (its meaning, in `CS_AFW360`) and to
a **representation**: either a codelist of allowed values or a plain type such
as Double or String. That is why every country file has the same 37 columns,
with the same codes in them.

## 1. Dimensions: the 19-column key

Every combination of these 19 values must be unique in a dataset.

| Group | Dimension | Codelist | What it says |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Context** | `FREQ` | CL_FREQ (only `A`, annual) | how often |
| | `REF_AREA` | CL_AREA (`SEN`, `GNB`) | country, ISO3 |
| | `GEO` | CL_GEO (36 codes, e.g. `SN01`) | subnational area, or `_T` for the whole country |
| | `ESTIMATION` | CL_ESTIMATION | `SURVEY` or `MODEL` |
| **What** | `INDICATOR` | CL_INDICATOR (62 codes) | e.g. `POV_HC`, `AGR_CULTIVATES` |
| **Who (fixed breakdowns)** | `SEX`, `AGE`, `URBANISATION` | CL_SEX, CL_AGE, CL_URBANISATION | standard SDMX breakdowns |
| **Who (flexible breakdowns)** | `COMP_BREAKDOWN_1…5` | CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN (61 codes) | e.g. `QUINT_Q1`, `DEC_MKT_D03`; `_T` if unused |
| **How it is measured** | `MEASURE_QUAL_1…5` | CL_QUALIFIER (43 codes) | welfare aggregate, poverty line, PPP round, etc.; `_Z` if unused |
| **When** | `TIME_PERIOD` (time dimension) | GregorianYear | a 4-digit year |

The main design choice is the **two groups of five "slot" dimensions**:

- **`COMP_BREAKDOWN_n`** splits the population: by quintile, decile, sex or
  age of the household head, poverty status, employment sector, and so on.
- **`MEASURE_QUAL_n`** changes the definition of the indicator: which poverty
  line, which PPP round, which welfare concept.

Slots are filled left to right in a fixed `slot_order`. This keeps the key the
same width for every indicator: adding a new kind of breakdown or qualifier
means adding codes to a codelist, not changing the DSD.

The two "nothing" codes mean different things:

- `_T` means "total", i.e. not broken down.
- `_Z` means "not applicable". For example, `SEX=_Z` on a household-level
  indicator.

## 2. Measures: the numbers (9)

The DSD uses SDMX 3.x multiple measures, so one row can carry a value and its
precision statistics:

- `OBS_VALUE` is mandatory. It is unrounded and in base units, so rates are
  shares between 0 and 1. It is `NaN` when `OBS_STATUS` is `O` or `M`.
- The other eight are optional (`minValue="0"` where a negative value makes no
  sense):
  - `STD_ERR`, `CI_LOWER`, `CI_UPPER`: sampling error and the 95% confidence
    interval.
  - `N_OBS`, `N_POP`, `N_OBS_NUM`: unweighted records, weighted population,
    and numerator records for shares.
  - `DEFF`, `DF`: design effect and degrees of freedom.

They are optional in the DSD, but the project validator requires them on
`PRODUCER`-source rows. Today's rows all come from converting the legacy
workbooks, so these columns are empty.

## 3. Attributes: describe a number, don't identify it (6)

| Attribute | Usage | Attached to | Representation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SERIES_ID` | mandatory | INDICATOR + the 10 slot dimensions | String, e.g. `POV_HC.POVLINE_PL300.PPP_2021` |
| `UNIT_MEASURE` | mandatory | REF_AREA + INDICATOR | CL_UNIT_MEASURE (`SHARE`, `LCU`, `PPP_USD`, `HA`…) |
| `OBS_STATUS` | mandatory | observation, linked to `OBS_VALUE` | CL_OBS_STATUS (`A`, `E`, `O`, `M`…) |
| `SOURCE_ID` | mandatory | observation | CL_SOURCE (the program run that produced the row) |
| `PRECISION` | optional | observation | Double, the rounding unit (e.g. `0.01` for legacy values) |
| `OBS_COMMENT` | optional | observation | free text |

What each `AttributeRelationship` means:

- **`SERIES_ID`** depends only on the "what and how" dimensions, not on
  country, area or year. It is the readable series name the dashboard matches
  on. It is a plain string, not a codelist, because SDMX IDs cannot contain
  dots.
- **`UNIT_MEASURE`** depends on the country as well as the indicator, because
  local currency (`LCU`) resolves to that country's ISO 4217 code.
- **`OBS_STATUS`** has a `MeasureRelationship` to `OBS_VALUE`: the status
  describes the main value, not the standard error.

## A real row, read through the DSD

From `30-sdmx/data/AFW360_HH_SEN_2021_SURVEY.csv`:

```
dataflow, WB.AFW360:AFW360_HH(0.3.0), R,
A, SEN, SN01, SURVEY, POV_HC, _T,_T,_T, _T,_T,_T,_T,_T, POVLINE_PL420,PPP_2021,_Z,_Z,_Z, 2021,   ← key
0.03, ,,,,,,,,                                                                                      ← measures
POV_HC.POVLINE_PL420.PPP_2021, SHARE, 0.01, A, SEN_EHCVM2021_LEGACY_v1,                           ← attributes
```

Read through the DSD: in **Senegal, region SN01**, the **survey-based poverty
headcount** at the **$4.20 line, 2021 PPP**, for the whole population (no
breakdowns) in **2021**, is **0.03 (3%)**. It is a **share**, rounded to
**0.01**, the status is **normal** (`A`), and it was produced by the **legacy
EHCVM 2021 conversion**.

The first three columns are SDMX-CSV 2.1 bookkeeping:

- `STRUCTURE=dataflow` says the next column names a dataflow.
- `STRUCTURE_ID` names the dataflow `AFW360_HH`, which points to this DSD.
- `ACTION=R` means "replace".

## How the DSD connects to the rest of the file

```
AgencyScheme (WB → AFW360)
   └─ ConceptScheme CS_AFW360 ──┐  meaning of each column
   └─ 22 Codelists ─────────────┤  allowed values
                                ▼
            DataStructure DSD_AFW360_HH        ← the schema
                                ▲
            Dataflow AFW360_HH ─┘              ← "this dataset uses that DSD" (named in every CSV row)
                                ▲
            ProvisionAgreement PA_AFW360_HH    ← data provider AFW_POV supplies that dataflow
```

The file also has a separate **Metadata Structure** (MSD) and
**Metadataflow**. They describe the reference metadata for surveys, sources,
text and figures (`30-sdmx/output/metadata/MDS_*.csv`), not the observations. That is
also why some codelists, such as `CL_SURVEY`, `CL_THEME`, `CL_STATISTIC` and
`CL_FIGURE`, are not used by any DSD dimension.

## Caveats

- Every artefact is version `0.3.0` and the codes are still `DRAFT`.
  `WB.AFW360` is a local placeholder agency until the structures are
  registered with the World Bank.
- Fusion Metadata Registry 12.4.2 rejects SDMX-ML 3.1, so this DSD is loaded
  into FMR with `--sdmx-ml-version 3.0`. The DSD loads, but the MSD, the
  metadataflow and the metadata provision agreement are left out, so the
  metadata files are not checked in FMR.
- To change the DSD, edit `30-sdmx/data/metadata/structure/DSD_AFW360_HH.csv` (named in the
  `AFW_SOURCE_FILE` annotation) and regenerate the XML with `build_sdmx.R`.
